proof.text: *Step 1 (finitely many affine triples).* Write $g_0:Y_0\to S_0$ for the structure morphism of $Y_0$ (so $g_0\circ f_0$ is that of $X_0$), $p_i:S\to S_i$ for the projections of the limit, and $t_{ii'}$ ($i\ge i'$) for the transition morphisms, $t_{00}=\mathrm{id}$. Let $x\in X_0$. Choose an affine open $W\subseteq S_0$ containing $g_0(f_0(x))$, an affine open $V\subseteq g_0^{-1}(W)$ containing $f_0(x)$, and an affine open $U\subseteq f_0^{-1}(V)$ containing $x$ (every point has an affine open neighbourhood inside any given open neighbourhood: [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] identifies an affine open with a spectrum, whose principal opens $D(h)$ form a basis of affine opens). Since $X_0$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], finitely many such triples $(W_b,V_b,U_b)$, $b=1,\dots,m$, satisfy $X_0=\bigcup_bU_b$, $f_0(U_b)\subseteq V_b$, $g_0(V_b)\subseteq W_b$. (The source covers $Y_0$ first and then each $f_0^{-1}(Y_{j,0})$; the triples above are the same data.) Put $A_0^b=\mathcal O_{S_0}(W_b)$, $B_0^b=\mathcal O_{Y_0}(V_b)$, $C_0^b=\mathcal O_{X_0}(U_b)$, with the ring maps $A_0^b\to B_0^b$ induced by $g_0$ and $\varphi_0^b:B_0^b\to C_0^b$ induced by $f_0$, a homomorphism of $A_0^b$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], under the identifications $W_b=\operatorname{Spec}A_0^b$, $V_b=\operatorname{Spec}B_0^b$, $U_b=\operatorname{Spec}C_0^b$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], the restrictions $U_b\to V_b\to W_b$ of $f_0$ and $g_0$ are $\operatorname{Spec}$ of these ring maps. Since $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation, $\varphi_0^b$ is of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. (Only the quasi-compactness of $X_0$ is used; the quasi-separatedness in Situation 081D is not needed here.)

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma Tag 04AI (lemma-descend-flat-finite-presentation, line 1868), first paragraph: finite affine open coverings of $Y_0$ and of $f_0^{-1}Y_{j,0}$

proof.text: *Step 2 (the base over $W_b$ as a colimit of rings).* Fix $b$ and drop it from the notation. For $i\ge0$ put $W_i=t_{i0}^{-1}(W)\subseteq S_i$, an affine open since $t_{i0}$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and $A_i=\mathcal O_{S_i}(W_i)$. For $i\ge i'\ge0$, $t_{ii'}$ maps $W_i$ into $W_{i'}$ and induces a ring map $A_{i'}\to A_i$; these form a directed system of rings over the directed set $I_{\ge0}=\{i\in I:i\ge0\}$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] the restricted transition morphism $W_i\to W_{i'}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A_{i'}\to A_i)$. Let $A=\varinjlim_{i\ge0}A_i$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and $W_S=p_0^{-1}(W)\subseteq S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] (clause on open subschemes of a stage, with $U_0=W$), $W_S$ with the restricted projections is the limit of $(W_i)_{i\ge0}$; by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] so is $\operatorname{Spec}A$ with the morphisms induced by the coprojections. By uniqueness of limits there is an isomorphism $W_S\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ under which $p_0|_{W_S}:W_S\to W$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(A_0\to A)$.

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma Tag 04AI, 'In the affine case we reduce to the following algebra result. Suppose that $R=\colim R_i$'; Situation Tag 081D (line 1739)

proof.text: *Step 3 (the pieces of $f_T$ are spectra).* Let $T$ be either $S_i$ for some $i\ge0$, with $q=t_{i0}$, $W_T=W_i$, $A_T=A_i$, or $S$, with $q=p_0$, $W_T=W_S$, $A_T=A$ (step 2); in both cases $W_T=q^{-1}(W)=\operatorname{Spec}A_T$ over $W=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$. Let $X_T=X_0\times_{S_0}T$, $Y_T=Y_0\times_{S_0}T$ with projections $\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2$ [def-pc-fibre-product] and $f_T=f_0\times\mathrm{id}_T$ (so $f_T=f_i$ for $T=S_i$, $f_T=f$ for $T=S$). Put $U_T=\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(U)\subseteq X_T$ and $V_T=\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(V)\subseteq Y_T$. Since $q\circ\mathrm{pr}_2=g_0f_0\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$ maps $U_T$ into $W$, $\mathrm{pr}_2(U_T)\subseteq W_T$, so $U_T=\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(U)\cap\mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(W_T)$, and [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] identifies $U_T$ with $U\times_WW_T$ compatibly with the projections; by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] $U_T\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_T\otimes_{A_0}C_0)$, the projections becoming $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $c\mapsto1\otimes c$ and $a\mapsto a\otimes1$ (the swap $C_0\otimes_{A_0}A_T\cong A_T\otimes_{A_0}C_0$ is the symmetry of $\otimes$). In the same way $V_T\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_T\otimes_{A_0}B_0)$. Since $\mathrm{pr}_1\circ f_T=f_0\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$ and $f_0(U)\subseteq V$, $f_T(U_T)\subseteq V_T$; the restriction $f_T|:U_T\to V_T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathrm{id}_{A_T}\otimes\varphi_0)$ are two morphisms into $V_T\cong V\times_WW_T$ with the same components ($f_0|_U\circ\mathrm{pr}_1$, as $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varphi_0)(1\otimes b)=1\otimes\varphi_0(b)$ and $f_0|_U=\operatorname{Spec}\varphi_0$ by step 1; and $\mathrm{pr}_2$, as $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\varphi_0)(a\otimes1)=a\otimes1$), hence equal by the universal property of the fibre product. So, up to these isomorphisms, $f_T|:U_T\to V_T$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $\varphi_T=\mathrm{id}_{A_T}\otimes\varphi_0:A_T\otimes_{A_0}B_0\to A_T\otimes_{A_0}C_0$. For $T=S_i$ the opens $U^b_{S_i}$, $b=1,\dots,m$, cover $X_i$, being preimages of the covering $X_0=\bigcup_bU_b$.

proof.text: *Step 4 (the hypothesis on the piece over $S$).* Take $T=S$ in step 3 and put $B=A\otimes_{A_0}B_0$, $C=A\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_A\otimes\varphi_0$. By [def-weil-flat-morphism], $f$ is flat at every $x\in X$: $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y,f(x)}$. The local rings of an open subscheme are those of the ambient scheme [def-pc-scheme], so for $x\in U_S$ the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{V_S,f(x)}\to\mathcal O_{U_S,x}$ of $f|:U_S\to V_S$ is that of $f$; hence $f|$ is flat. Isomorphisms $\alpha:\operatorname{Spec}C\to U_S$, $\beta:V_S\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi=\beta\circ f|\circ\alpha$ (step 3) identify the local homomorphism of $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ at a point $z$ with that of $f|$ at $\alpha(z)$ through ring isomorphisms, so $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi:\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine], $\varphi$ is a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma Tag 04AI: 'Since the property of being flat is local' and the hypothesis 'If $R\otimes_{R_0}A_0\to R\otimes_{R_0}B_0$ is flat'

proof.text: *Step 5 (the algebra fact).* By steps 1, 2 and 4, the directed system $(A_i)_{i\ge0}$ with colimit $A$, the index $0$ and the $A_0$-algebra homomorphism of finite presentation $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ satisfy the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-flat-ring-map] over the directed set $I_{\ge0}$ (its $B,C,\varphi$ are those of step 4, and $\varphi$ is flat). So there is $i_b\ge0$ such that $\varphi_i=\mathrm{id}_{A_i}\otimes\varphi_0:A_i\otimes_{A_0}B_0\to A_i\otimes_{A_0}C_0$ is a flat ring map for every $i\ge i_b$.

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma Tag 04AI, second paragraph: 'This follows from Algebra, Lemma 02JO part (3)'

proof.text: *Step 6 (a common index; $f_i$ is flat).* $I$ is directed and there are finitely many $b$, so there is $i\in I$ with $i\ge0$ and $i\ge i_b$ for $b=1,\dots,m$. For each $b$, $\varphi^b_i$ is flat (step 5), so $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi^b_i$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]; by step 3 (with $T=S_i$) the restriction $f_i|:U^b_{S_i}\to V^b_{S_i}$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi^b_i$ up to isomorphisms of source and target, so as in step 4 it is flat at every point of $U^b_{S_i}$ [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Let $x\in X_i$; by step 3 $x\in U^b_{S_i}$ for some $b$, and since the local rings of the open subschemes $U^b_{S_i}\subseteq X_i$ and $V^b_{S_i}\subseteq Y_i$ are those of $X_i$ and $Y_i$ [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal O_{X_i,x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{Y_i,f_i(x)}$. Hence $f_i$ is flat.

title: Flatness descends to a finite stage of a limit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed set, with a chosen element $0$, and let $(S_i,t_{ii'})$ be an inverse system of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with affine transition morphisms $t_{ii'}:S_i\to S_{i'}$ for $i\ge i'$ [pqf-def-affine-morphism], with limit $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism over $S_0$, with $S_0,X_0,Y_0$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For $i\ge0$ put $X_i=X_0\times_{S_0}S_i$, $Y_i=Y_0\times_{S_0}S_i$ and $f_i=f_0\times\mathrm{id}_{S_i}$, and put $X=X_0\times_{S_0}S$, $Y=Y_0\times_{S_0}S$, $f=f_0\times\mathrm{id}_S$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. If $f$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and $f_0$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then $f_i$ is flat for some $i\ge0$.
